newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wide-screen TV sector needs more public money - EU.
newsitem.headline: Wide-screen TV sector needs more public money - EU.

text.p: The European Union market for wide-screen television is growing, but is not yet ready to operate without public money, the European Commission said on Thursday.
EU consumers have bought 500,000 wide-screen television sets and 39 broadcasters are now offering programmes in the new cinema-style format, the Commission said in a statement.
It gave the EU credit for boosting demand, saying that money it had provided for programme production and broadcasting costs had given viewers an incentive to buy the new TV sets.
However, the sector was not yet producing a "critical mass" of services that would allow it to survive without subsidies.
It said it was exploring whether the 15-member EU should extend the 228-million-Ecu ($290 million) "action plan" that it launched in 1993 to support programmes using a width-to-height ratio of 16:9.
"Wide-screen television may have now started in 13 member states, but it is still in its infancy in many of them," it said in a statement.

The EU adopted the four-year funding plan after it dropped a much more ambitious and controversial plan for helping Europe's high-definition television (HDTV) sector compete with Japan and the United States in the face of industry opposition.

The Commission said it had allocated 12.5 million Ecus ($15.9 million) in new money this week to help 23 broadcasters -- ranging from Britain's BSkyB and Germany's NDR to Ireland's RTE and Finland's TV Tampere -- transmit in the 16:9 format.
It said wide-screen TV was most popular in Germany, France and Belgium and that those countries might be able to do without public money after 1997.
"This will not yet be the case for the other member states," it said.
